candidates.summary: a []byte call argument now arrives with cap = base64.DecodedLen(len(arg)) instead of len(decoded), so ignored \r\n padding picks the slice's cap and the size of the array persisted, the malleability this file's header forbids
candidates.failure_scenario:
MsgCall to `func Probe(cur realm, b []byte) (int, int) { Stored = b; return len(b), cap(b) }` with arg "AAAA" returns (3, 3); with "AAAA



" returns (3, 6); with "AAAA" + 8x"
" returns (3, 15). NewSliceFromData takes data[:cap(data)] as the base array, and base64.DecodeString returns a buffer of DecodedLen(len(arg)), so one byte string has unboundedly many encodings that differ in realm-visible cap and in the zero-filled array a realm persists (a len check in the realm passes while cap, storage and the alloc charge grow with the padding). At the merge base all three return (3, 3).

candidates.summary: the new guard skips typed-nil slice/map/func keys as 'no Go constant' but misses the typed-nil pointer member of that class, which ComputeMapKey dedups: map[any]int{(*int)(nil): 1, (*int)(nil): 2} is now rejected at preprocess though Go and the merge base accept it
candidates.failure_scenario: A package with `m := map[any]int{(*int)(nil): 1, (*int)(nil): 2}` fails to preprocess with "duplicate key (nil *int) in map literal" at head; go run prints 1 and the merge base runs it. The same class's map[*int]int{nil: 1, nil: 2} is rejected at both head and base (pre-existing, Go accepts it). A realm using such a literal cannot be deployed. isComparable(*PointerType) is true, so the guard lets it through to the kset dedup; nil is not a Go constant, so Go never dedups it.
candidates.verify_by: cp tests/solo-finder-2-maplit-nil-f.gno gnovm/tests/files/sf2_maplit_nil_f.gno && go test ./gnovm/pkg/gnolang -run TestFiles/sf2_maplit_nil_f -count=1 -timeout 2m at head (unexpected panic: duplicate key (nil *int)) and at 6c49f5420 (ok); same for _b (fails at both).
